claims.text: As-cast eutectic Al0.7CoCrFeNi has a lamellar fcc+B2 structure.
Annealing as-cast Al0.7CoCrFeNi at 550°C for 1 hour under inert atmosphere will form fine, coherent L12 nanoprecipitates.
The L12 nanoprecipitates will be uniformly distributed within the fcc lamellae.
Fine L12 precipitates increase the strength of Al0.7CoCrFeNi.
Strengthening by the fine L12 precipitates occurs through Orowan dislocation bowing and bypass.
The coherence of the L12 precipitates preserves the fcc matrix's ability to accommodate strain and therefore maintains or enhances tensile ductility.
Deformation twinning may contribute to strain accommodation in the precipitate-containing alloy.
The as-cast baseline has a yield strength of approximately 1400 MPa.
The proposed annealing treatment will raise yield strength to more than 1800 MPa under quasi-static tensile testing.
The annealed alloy will retain tensile elongation of at least 15%.
Departures from 550°C for 1 hour may cause over-aging or precipitate coarsening that negates the strength-ductility benefits.
The treatment response is sensitive to the initial microstructure and the cooling rate after annealing.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts both yield strength above 1800 MPa and ductility at or above 15%, so failure of either endpoint should refute the stated quantitative prediction. The falsification rule instead requires both mechanical endpoints to fail simultaneously, allowing a result that violates one prediction to escape falsification.

The rule treats failure to exceed 1800 MPa as equivalent to absence of a statistically significant strength increase, although statistical significance and attainment of an absolute strength threshold are not equivalent.
